results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** developments $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data and a data-fixing isometric immersion $\varphi:M\to M'$ as in the statement.

[L1] Cauchy data: $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$ and $\Sigma'$ a Cauchy set of $M'$; $\varphi|_\Sigma:\Sigma\to\Sigma'$ is the diffeomorphism $j'\circ j^{-1}$; every maximal geodesic of $M$ with nonzero causal initial data is a causal curve that is inextendible in $M$, and it meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c), [[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clause (b), [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)).

[L2] Metric nondegeneracy and dimension: $g_p$ and $g'_q$ are nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on four-dimensional tangent spaces; if $v\in T_pM$ satisfies $d\varphi_pv=0$ then $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\varphi(p)}(0,d\varphi_pw)=0$ for every $w\in T_pM$, so $v=0$ by nondegeneracy ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)); consequently $d\varphi_p$ is injective, and it is an isomorphism because both tangent spaces have dimension $4$.

[L3] Isometric immersions map geodesics to geodesics with velocity $d\varphi(\gamma')$, so the images of the maximal geodesics through $p$ and through $q=\gamma(0)$ have the same velocity data after transport by $\varphi$; the maximal geodesic of $M'$ with given initial data is unique and its restriction to any subinterval is the unique geodesic with those data ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] step 1.1, [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clauses (a) and (d)).

[L4] An isomorphism of tangent spaces gives a local diffeomorphism by [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]].

[L5] Future data-fixing isometric immersions have identical initial differentials and obey connected-domain rigidity, by [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clauses (a)-(b). The identity map satisfies [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (b).

No choice principle is used in this item.



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Reduction to injectivity at two points.) Let $p,q\in M$ with $\varphi(p)=\varphi(q)=:z$. We show $p=q$. By [L2] the differential $d\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism, so $\varphi$ restricts to a diffeomorphism of some open neighbourhood $V$ of $p$ onto an open neighbourhood of $z$. [L2, L4, algebra]

1.2 (Two geodesics through $q$ and through $p$.) Choose a future-directed timelike vector $u\in T_qM$. By [L1] and [L3] there is a maximal geodesic $\gamma:I_\gamma\to M$ of $M$ with $\gamma(0)=q$, $\gamma'(0)=u$, which is a timelike curve, is inextendible in $M$, and meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value $\tau_0$. Its image $\varphi\circ\gamma$ is a geodesic of $M'$ with $(\varphi\circ\gamma)(0)=z$ and velocity $d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$; since $d\varphi_q$ is an isomorphism, define $w:=(d\varphi_p)^{-1}\bigl(d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))\bigr)\in T_pM$, a timelike vector, and let $\sigma:I_\sigma\to M$ be the maximal geodesic of $M$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, $\sigma'(0)=w$; it is timelike, inextendible in $M$, and meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value $\tau_1$. [L1, L2, L3, choose]

1.3 (The two image geodesics are the same maximal geodesic of $M'$.) By [L3] both $\varphi\circ\sigma$ and $\varphi\circ\gamma$ are geodesics of $M'$; at parameter $0$ both have value $z$ and velocity $d\varphi_p(w)=d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$. Let $\zeta:I_\zeta\to M'$ be the maximal geodesic of $M'$ with $\zeta(0)=z$, $\zeta'(0)=d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$ ([L3]). By uniqueness of maximal geodesics, $I_\sigma\subseteq I_\zeta$, $I_\gamma\subseteq I_\zeta$, $\varphi\circ\sigma=\zeta|_{I_\sigma}$ and $\varphi\circ\gamma=\zeta|_{I_\gamma}$. [L3, algebra]

2.1 (The initial-surface crossing parameters coincide.) By step 1.3 and [L1], $\varphi(\sigma(\tau_1))=\zeta(\tau_1)\in\Sigma'$ and $\varphi(\gamma(\tau_0))=\zeta(\tau_0)\in\Sigma'$, with $\tau_1\in I_\sigma\subseteq I_\zeta$ and $\tau_0\in I_\gamma\subseteq I_\zeta$. The geodesic $\zeta$ has timelike velocity, hence is a causal curve, and by [L3] it is inextendible in $M'$; since $\Sigma'$ is a Cauchy set of $M'$ ([L1]), the parameter set $\zeta^{-1}[\Sigma']$ has exactly one element. Hence $\tau_0=\tau_1$ and $\zeta(\tau_0)=\zeta(\tau_1)$. [step 1.3, L1, L3, algebra]

3.1 (Equal points and velocities on $\Sigma$.) By step 2.1, $\varphi(\sigma(\tau_0))=\varphi(\gamma(\tau_0))$ with both arguments in $\Sigma$; since $\varphi|_\Sigma=j'\circ j^{-1}$ is injective ([L1]), $\sigma(\tau_0)=\gamma(\tau_0)=:x$. Differentiating $\varphi\circ\sigma=\zeta=\varphi\circ\gamma$ at $\tau_0$ gives $d\varphi_x(\sigma'(\tau_0))=d\varphi_x(\gamma'(\tau_0))$, and $d\varphi_x$ is injective by [L2], so $\sigma'(\tau_0)=\gamma'(\tau_0)$. Hence $\sigma$ and $\gamma$ are maximal geodesics with the same value and velocity at $\tau_0$; by uniqueness [L3] they agree on the intersection of their intervals, which contains $0$, so $p=\sigma(0)=\gamma(0)=q$. [step 2.1, L2, L3, algebra]

4.1 (Clauses (a) and (b).) Clause (a) is [L2]. For clause (b): step 3.1 shows that $\varphi$ is injective; by clause (a) and the inverse function theorem on manifolds, $\varphi$ is a local diffeomorphism, hence an open map, so $\varphi(M)$ is open in $M'$ and $\varphi:M\to\varphi(M)$ is a bijective local diffeomorphism, hence a diffeomorphism; it satisfies the remaining clauses of a development embedding by hypothesis. [step 1.1, step 3.1, L2, L4, algebra]

5.1 (Clause (c).) Let $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ be data-fixing isometric immersions and let $M$ be connected. On every point $x\in\Sigma$ the two maps have the same value $j'$ and, by [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (b), the same differential; hence by rigidity (clause (a) of that lemma) $\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $M$. Taking $\psi_2=\mathrm{id}_M:M\to M$ (which is data-fixing by [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (b)) gives the self-isometry statement. [step 4.1, L5, algebra] ∎



Clause (b) shows that in the definition of an extension of a development one
need not require the map to be an embedding: a data-fixing isometric immersion
is automatically one. Clause (c) is the uniqueness used at the end of
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]]; its connectedness
hypothesis is the one of [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (a).

**Given:** Countable Choice, Dependent Choice, two developments $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data, with $\Sigma=j(\Sigma)$ Cauchy in both.

[L1] Common subdevelopments form a set: a common subdevelopment is a pair $(U,\varphi)$ with $U\subseteq M$ and $\varphi:U\to M'$; since $U$ is an element of the power set of $M$ and the graph of $\varphi$ is an element of the power set of $M\times M'$, the collection of all common subdevelopments is a set by separation ([[def-power-set]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]).

[L2] Restriction and gluing of development data: each $U_\alpha$ is open, is a development of the same data with the restricted fields, and $\psi_\alpha$ is a development embedding, hence in particular an isometric immersion fixing the data and the time orientation ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a), [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c)).

[L3] Agreement on overlaps is [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (c). Nonemptiness follows from the local complete-data uniqueness theorem for the selected fixed model: the admissible fixed coupled-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] (including its vacuum instance), [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] or a specified independent reduction, including the tilted nonnegative dust theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. With their Countable Choice and Dependent Choice assumptions, two developments agree near the entire initial surface by a future data-fixing isometry matching all matter fields. Apply the intrinsic Cauchy-neighborhood construction [[lem-gr-local-cauchy-neighborhood]] to a smaller common isometry collar, and transport that neighborhood by the isometry. Its source and image have the entire initial surface Cauchy, so this restriction is a common subdevelopment.

[L4] Portion inextendibility and Cauchy property: if a causal curve is inextendible in $U^*$, then for every component $J$ of its preimage under one of the sets $U_\alpha$ the restriction is inextendible in $U_\alpha$ ([[lem-gr-portion-inextendibility]]); and every causal curve inextendible in $U_\alpha$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)5).

[L5] Two crossings in the ambient development: if a causal curve in $M$ met $\Sigma$ in two distinct parameter values, then by the segment-extension clause the compact segment between them lies on an inextendible causal curve of $M$ meeting $\Sigma$ twice, contradicting that $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$ ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clause (c), [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c), [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

[L6] Local differential geometry on $U^*$: a map whose restriction to an open cover of its domain is a smooth isometric immersion is a smooth isometric immersion, and the field equations of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)4 are local, so they hold on $U^*$; injectivity of a data-fixing isometric immersion of developments follows from [[lem-gr-data-fixing-immersion-is-embedding]] clause (b).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (The union and the patched map.) Let $\{(U_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be the set of all common subdevelopments, which exists by [L1] and is nonempty by [L3]. Put $U^*:=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha$, an open subset of $M$ containing $j(\Sigma)$; define $\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ by $\psi^*(p):=\psi_\alpha(p)$ for $p\in U_\alpha$. This is well defined by [L3]: if $p\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$, then $\psi_\alpha(p)=\psi_\beta(p)$. [L1, L3, construct]

2.1 ($U^*$ is a development with Cauchy surface $\Sigma$.) Let $\gamma:I\to U^*$ be a future causal curve inextendible in $U^*$, choose $t_0\in I$ with $\gamma(t_0)\in U_{\alpha_0}$, and let $J$ be the connected component of $\gamma^{-1}[U_{\alpha_0}]$ containing $t_0$. By [L4] the restriction $\gamma|_J$ is inextendible in $U_{\alpha_0}$ and therefore meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value of $J\subseteq I$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ at least once. If it met $\Sigma$ at two distinct parameter values, then by [L5] applied in $M$ this would contradict that $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value, and the same holds for past causal curves by the time reverse. Thus $(U^*,g|_{U^*},N|_{U^*},j,\psi|_{U^*})$ is a development of the same data: it is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with $j(\Sigma)$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface (as $U^*$ is open in $M$), the field equations hold by [L6], the induced data are those of $j$ and $\psi$, and $\Sigma$ is Cauchy by the above. [step 1.1, L2, L4, L5, L6, algebra]

3.1 ($\psi^*$ is a data-fixing development embedding.) By [L2] each $\psi_\alpha$ is an isometric immersion fixing the data and the time orientation; these are local properties, so $\psi^*$ is a smooth isometric immersion with $\psi^*\circ j=j'$ and $g'_{\psi^*(p)}(d\psi^*_pN_p,N'_{\psi^*(p)})<0$ for every $p\in U^*$, matching every matter field by [L2]. Hence $\psi^*$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $U^*$ into $M'$; by [L6] it is injective and therefore a data-fixing development embedding. So $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment, which is clause (a). [step 2.1, L2, L6, algebra]

4.1 (Universality.) Every $(U_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$ satisfies $U_\alpha\subseteq U^*$ by definition of the union, and $\psi^*|_{U_\alpha}=\psi_\alpha$ by definition of $\psi^*$; in particular the pair $(U^*,\psi^*)$ satisfies the universal property of clause (b), and $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U^*$ by step 1.1. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (Uniqueness.) Let $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ also satisfy (a) and (b). Since $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ is itself one of the common subdevelopments, (b) applied to $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ gives $U^\dagger\subseteq U^*$; conversely (b) for $(U^*,\psi^*)$ applied to $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ gives $U^*\subseteq U^\dagger$. Hence $U^\dagger=U^*$, and then for every $p\in U^*$ the two maps agree because $p$ lies in some common subdevelopment $(U_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$ and both $\psi^\dagger$ and $\psi^*$ restrict to $\psi_\alpha$ there. This is clause (c). [step 4.1, algebra] ∎



The construction is Sbierski's; the only structural ingredients are the agreement of the maps on overlaps ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (c)), the fact that a maximal connected portion of an inextendible curve inside one member remains inextendible there ([[lem-gr-portion-inextendibility]]), and the acyclicity of "two crossings of a Cauchy set" ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clause (c)). No Zorn's lemma and no selection of representatives of isometry classes is used.
